bug_semantics: A routing message can select a definition that composes the routing function with itself. The catalog returns a composed FunctionInvocationWrapper whose target is a composition lambda, so RoutingFunction's direct-target self check does not recognize it as the router; applying the wrapper invokes the router again on the same input, producing unbounded recursion and eventual OOM denial of service.
flaw_origin: Commit 4d9cdb9750ceba2bfc634b03b77dc82494742269 added and auto-registered the header-directed RoutingFunction without rejecting a route back to itself or a composition containing itself. Its parent already supported Function-to-Function composition via function1.andThen(function2), so adding this recursively selectable function was the smallest commit that first made the mechanism vulnerable. The later 2023 direct-target guard was incomplete because a composed wrapper has a different target.
ai_marker: absent: BIC author and committer are Oleg Zhurakousky <ozhurakousky@pivotal.io>; the full commit message has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI marker
evidence: Vendor advisory https://spring.io/security/cve-2026-40989 names 'Self Routing guard bypassed via function composition', states that infinite routing recursion can cause OOM, and prescribes avoiding self-composition when upgrade is impossible; it lists OSS fixes 4.3.3 and 5.0.2 and enterprise fixes 3.2.16, 4.1.10, and 4.2.6.
The CVE.org record from https://cveawg.mitre.org/api/cve/CVE-2026-40989 is PUBLISHED, repeats the uncontrolled-recursion/OOM mechanism and affected version families, and is not rejected or withdrawn.

git show 4d9cdb9750ceba2bfc634b03b77dc82494742269 adds RoutingFunction.java (105 lines) and the conditional 'router' bean registration; RoutingFunction obtains a header-selected name, calls functionCatalog.lookup(routeToFunctionName), and applies the returned function without cycle validation.

git show abeb6528305f3c5186cbd34583cf129f6b50410a:.../AbstractComposableFunctionRegistry.java shows the parent already composed two Function registrations with function1.andThen(function2); git cat-file -e abeb6528305f3c5186cbd34583cf129f6b50410a:.../RoutingFunction.java fails because the routing function is absent from the immediate parent.

git show e3a44c3cf30d3719d95c0225e7c72e6ca731ae3d adds the 2023 check function.getTarget().equals(this); pre-fix RoutingFunction still accepts a spring.cloud.function.definition header and applies the returned wrapper, while a composition's target is not the router itself.

git show 6bcd55803c5a2ce0adec794fee1e03c2fac36cf9 adds FunctionInvocationWrapper equality by functionDefinition and rejects this.equals(after) in andThen, with testCompositionWithItself; this directly blocks functionRouter|functionRouter composition.

Tag ancestry checks show BIC 4d9cdb9750ceba2bfc634b03b77dc82494742269 is contained in vulnerable v4.3.2 and v5.0.1 and in patched v4.3.3 and v5.0.2; fix 6bcd55803c5a2ce0adec794fee1e03c2fac36cf9 is contained in v4.3.3 but not v4.3.2, and sibling fix 57b4a1c05a48bb4240026e33bc05f2395ed5576c is contained in v5.0.2 but not v5.0.1.

git show --format=fuller 4d9cdb9750ceba2bfc634b03b77dc82494742269 reports one parent, human author/committer Oleg Zhurakousky, and a conventional GH-238 commit message with no AI-related trailer or bot identity.
reasoning: The vulnerable lifecycle starts when 4d9cdb9750ceba2bfc634b03b77dc82494742269 introduces a catalog-registered router into a catalog that already permits arbitrary Function composition. The immediate parent cannot self-route because RoutingFunction.java and its bean do not exist there, satisfying the parent-absence gate. A 2023 guard prevents lookup of the bare router target but not a composed wrapper such as functionRouter|functionRouter, whose lambda target passes that check and re-enters routing. The advisory-linked 6bcd55803c5a2ce0adec794fee1e03c2fac36cf9 closes the bypass at the composition primitive by rejecting two wrappers with the same definition; public tag ancestry aligns that fix with 4.3.3, and its sibling aligns with 5.0.2. Because the atomic BIC is a normal human-authored commit with no commit-object AI marker, this real vulnerability is NOT_AI.
